advice: Abstain. The supplied evidence does not support a distinct, bounded scratch-lifetime change that preserves the fixed kernel. The prior 64 KiB proposal was incompatible with the existing 256-byte K-slice stride, consumer rewinds, and two-half traversal. A valid smaller-buffer design needs coordinated changes to packing, strides, addressing, and traversal; proposing it without the exact source and a complete mapping risks out-of-bounds reads or incorrect output. No performance benefit is established.
risks: The evidence does not include a source and call flow sufficient to specify a safe coordinated redesign or verify stack lifetime. Avoid inferring that reducing the buffer improves speed from its size alone; earlier scratch-layout scores were noisy and did not promote a gain.
